newsitem.title: ESTONIA: INACTIVE BOURSE STABLE TO SLIGHTLY LOWER.
newsitem.headline: INACTIVE BOURSE STABLE TO SLIGHTLY LOWER.

text.p: * Morning trade was 14.5 million kroons on Wednesday on the
Estonian bourse.
* The Talse on-line index was down 0.02 percent to 276.01.
* Hoiupank was the most active stock with 6.4
million kroons traded to be higher at 151.35/151.70 vs 151.25
kroons.
* Hansapank registered 4.4 million kroons on a
higher spread of 147.25/147.40 vs 147.15 kroons.
* Dealers said the the market was mostly inactive with some
temporary buying interest in Hansapank and Hoiupank showing
support for a stable bourse rather than pushing prices higher.
(See index on stock exchange web site:
http://www.tse.ee/online/total.htm)
Estonian shares were stable on Wednesday morning as temporary buying interest kept prices steady ahead of the banking sector's June and first half results, dealers said.
"Longer-term investors seem to be helping keep prices stable but selling pressure is being felt in almost all stocks," one trader said.
Dealers expected prices and volumes to remain stable in the lead up to June and half-year results.
Hoiupank was higher on 151.35/151.70 kroons compared to 151.25 kroons with volume of 6.3 million kroons.
Hansapank's spread was 147.25/147.70 kroons against 147.15 kroons on turnover of 2.4 million kroons.
"There is still a bit of life in the merger rumours involving Hoiupank and Tallinna Pank, and this could be still affecting the interest in Hoiupank," another dealer said.
Newspaper reports last week said that Hoiupank was considering merger talks with Tallinna Pank and this news helped fuel trade in the banking sector during the three-day week.
Trade on the free market remained quiet with no volume over half a million kroons.
-- David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom, +372 620 9202, reuters@reuters.ee
